title: Aisha · Contact and an ending
orientation: Non-acute moments about wanting contact and facing a bounded ending. No promise of constant availability or deeper disclosure is required. Use the prompted skill, give feedback and retry. Each scene is another moment, not a response to your exact words.

scenes.bridge: Aisha begins with what a glance away can mean to her.
scenes.prompt: Reflect the fear without promising uninterrupted attention.
scenes.text: [Panicked] If you look away while I am talking, even to check a note, I panic that you are losing interest. Then I start talking faster, adding details, anything to keep you with me.
scenes.suggestion: When I look away, you panic that I am losing interest and try harder to keep my attention.

scenes.bridge: She asks whether her feelings can have a place in the work.
scenes.text: [Worried] What if my feelings are too much for any therapist to work with?
scenes.suggestion: You worry that your feelings will be too much, even here. We can begin with a small part and notice what helps or makes it harder. That helps us choose the pace and support you need, rather than ask you to bring everything at once.

scenes.bridge: Another appointment brings fear around the door.
scenes.prompt: Validate the alarm without treating it as proof of leaving.
scenes.text: [Panicked] I watched the door most of session to make sure you won't leave. Every time the hallway got quiet, I thought this might be the moment you decide I am too much and walk out.
scenes.suggestion: After so many abrupt endings, it is understandable to fear being left again. That fear deserves care; you do not have to dismiss it just because it shows up here too.

scenes.bridge: She describes opposing wishes arriving quickly.
scenes.prompt: Ask about the shift without choosing the correct wish.
scenes.text: [Desperate] I go from please do not leave to leave me alone in seconds.
scenes.suggestion: Just before it flips, what feeling is too painful to remain near?

scenes.bridge: Another moment stays near the confusion in those wishes.
scenes.prompt: Explore both with room to slow down.
scenes.text: [Confused and embarrassed] I can ask someone not to leave and then want them away from me seconds later. I do not understand which part is actually me.
scenes.suggestion: Both movements are there: reaching and pushing away. What changes inside in the seconds between asking them to stay and wanting them gone?

scenes.bridge: A clock glance brings an unspoken meaning.
scenes.prompt: Offer a tentative guess and check fit.
scenes.text: [Desperate] If you glance at the clock, my stomach drops like you are already leaving me.
scenes.suggestion: That glance becomes a leaving signal; I wonder if underneath the drop is a fear that you stop mattering once someone turns away.

scenes.bridge: Hurt in a pause shifts toward doing the exercise quickly.
scenes.prompt: Invite a look at the pause rather than push the task.
scenes.text: [Hurt, then dismisses] That pause felt awful. Fine, let’s just do the exercise.
scenes.suggestion: Before the exercise, could we understand what felt awful in our pause?

scenes.bridge: Aisha recalls an abrupt ending in an earlier appointment.
scenes.prompt: Acknowledge the impact and plan a bounded ending together.
scenes.text: [Desperate] When the session ended exactly on time, it felt like you dropped me. I know there has to be a clock, but the way it happened made me feel like the connection disappeared the second the hour was over.
scenes.suggestion: When we ended, you felt the connection disappear. I am sorry the ending felt so abrupt. I need to keep the time limit, and we can leave room before it to check how you are and what support you need until we meet again.

scenes.bridge: A later moment holds needing contact and shame about the need.
scenes.prompt: Stay present without promising unlimited contact.
scenes.text: [Desperate] I feel like I am too much, and I hate that I need you to stay.
scenes.suggestion: The need for me feels unbearable and shameful at the same time. I can sit with that exposed needing for a moment without treating you as too much.

scenes.bridge: Another calm moment brings relief and uncertainty about herself.
scenes.prompt: Reflect the mix without requiring a crisis or a conclusion.
scenes.text: [Low voice] When things are calm, I don't know who I am. I'm relieved nobody is leaving, but I feel empty and almost miss having something to fight about.
scenes.suggestion: The calm brings relief, but also an emptiness that leaves you unsure of who you are.

scenes.bridge: Aisha notices two truths about the hour ending.
scenes.prompt: Help her name both without asking her to like the ending.
scenes.text: [Quiet, uncertain] I can want the hour to continue and know it ends. I don’t like it.
scenes.suggestion: What makes room for both today, without asking you to like the ending?

scenes.bridge: The imagined hour has a few minutes left.
scenes.prompt: Name time plainly and agree how to use it.
scenes.text: [Upset, present] We’re nearly done. I need to hear that plainly, not notice you packing up.
scenes.suggestion: We have a few minutes left. I’m here for them; let’s agree how to use them for ending.
